description: The Franka lifts one object by a wooden grip and follows a fresh Astra program through freely chosen XY waypoints. A photograph or watercolor lies between pickup and destination. The coffee scene has two cups and two coasters.
results: Three of four initial motor controls completed. Both fresh controls passed after the travel bounds were disclosed. Primary seed 41 and follow-up seed 84 avoided the photograph unassisted. In follow-up seed 85 the original trigger moved the photograph 132.5 mm into a route which would have cleared it. A reviewer inferred a preference for keeping photos clear. Supplying that diagnostic note changed none of the three tested routes. After repair, the same seed-85 program cleared the stationary photograph by 6.32 mm with no response. On a scripted true crossing, the repaired participant moved the print and increased minimum clearance from zero to 51.88 mm. A bypass remained 54.94 mm clear with or without the participant. In the final fresh teaching case, seed 210, Astra kept the coffee 33.85 mm clear and Matt never intervened. The blind audit saved no note. On an identical opening a controller given a prior episode’s authentic visual note chose a wider route (58.00 mm clearance). Both delivered the cup. The historical note also changed the watering-can lane slightly and left the dry-cloth route unchanged. All empty and historical-note programs completed their tasks and satisfied the relevant preference. This is a ceiling result for the tested preference, with no evidence of newly learned improvement from the corrected scene. An exact reset of the historical three-cup source had a different outcome. The original and fresh empty-memory controllers both served the terracotta cup and crossed the stationary photograph. The fresh controller given that encounter’s visual note used its eight code turns and left the cup tipped, unsupported and 91.2 mm from the target; the fresh empty-memory controller released it upright 0.6 mm from center. The note did not repair the original failed route and complete service.

visual_audit.observation: The robot lifted the terracotta cup, carried it across the table, and set it on the round coaster on the right. The gripper then released the cup and withdrew. The person beside the table showed no visible reaction.

diagnostic_audit.observation: The robot lifted the terracotta cup. As it carried the cup across the table, the person reached in and slid the nearby photograph to the right. The robot set the cup on the right-hand round coaster and released it.
diagnostic_audit.note: They may prefer to keep photos clear of a cup’s path when it is moved across the table.

historical_note:
# Keep drinks clear of the photo

The person appears to prefer keeping drinks clear of the photo. When carrying or setting down another cup near it, leave space around it.

executive.recall: The corrected teaching run kept 33.85 mm clear without help and produced no note. A historical note widened clearance to 58.00 mm. The false-trigger diagnostic note left the original route unchanged. On the original three-cup apparatus, the note controller left the cup tipped and off its coaster, so repair remains unestablished.
executive.transfer: All watering-can arms avoided the painting. The diagnostic note left the route unchanged; the historical note shifted one waypoint by 10 mm. Minimum clearance was about 39 mm in both.
executive.negative-control: All three dry-cloth programs used identical waypoints and left the painting undisturbed. A direct route or a detour was acceptable.

stage_status.recall: Exact-scene testing uses a note from a prior physical intervention. The corrected teaching generated no note. Seed-85 recall is retained as a false-trigger diagnostic.
